AnalyticsExportRows.description:
Body of ``GET /analytics/{report}/export?format=json``.

The rows the CSV would carry, each serialised exactly as in the report.
AnalyticsExportRows.title: AnalyticsExportRows

AnalyticsPeriod.description: Bucket width of a time series.
AnalyticsPeriod.title: AnalyticsPeriod

AuditRecordOut.description: One entry as the API publishes it.
AuditRecordOut.title: AuditRecordOut

AuthPayload.description: Body of a successful login or refresh.
AuthPayload.title: AuthPayload

AuthenticatedUser.description:
The signed-in account as the client sees it.

The permission list is flattened across every role the user holds because
the client builds its navigation and its per-record affordances from this
array alone.
AuthenticatedUser.title: AuthenticatedUser

BankStatementOut.description: A statement as the API publishes it.
BankStatementOut.title: BankStatementOut

BankTransactionDetailOut.description:
One transaction, read on its own, with whatever it might belong to.

``candidates`` is empty for anything the rule already settled — a matched
line has an answer, and an unmatched one had none to offer.
BankTransactionDetailOut.title: BankTransactionDetailOut

BankTransactionOut.description: One line of a statement, and how far it got towards an order.
BankTransactionOut.title: BankTransactionOut

CallOut.description:
A call as the API publishes it.

``deletedAt`` is deliberately absent: a soft-deleted record never leaves the
service, so the flag would only ever be null on the wire.
CallOut.title: CallOut

CallRecordingOut.description:
A playable link to the recording, and the moment it stops working.

The link is short-lived on purpose: a recording is a conversation with a
customer, and a URL that never expires is one that keeps working long after
the person who was shown it stopped being allowed to hear it.
CallRecordingOut.title: CallRecordingOut

CircuitState.description: The three positions of the breaker in front of the upstream.
CircuitState.title: CircuitState

ContactOut.description:
A contact as the API publishes it.

``deleted_at`` is deliberately absent: a soft-deleted record never leaves
the service, so the flag would only ever be null on the wire.
ContactOut.title: ContactOut

ContactSortField.description:
Columns a client may order the collection by.

An enum rather than a free string: ``sortBy`` ends up in an ``ORDER BY``
clause, and accepting whatever arrives would make that clause caller-written
SQL. The values are the wire spelling, the service maps them to columns.
ContactSortField.title: ContactSortField

CreateDealRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /deals``.

``stage`` is accepted only as the literal ``LEAD``: a deal has to start at
the beginning of the pipeline, and allowing anything else on creation would
be a way around the machine.
CreateDealRequest.title: CreateDealRequest

CreateShipmentRequest.description: Books a previously quoted parcel with the carrier.
CreateShipmentRequest.title: CreateShipmentRequest

CreateTicketRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /helpdesk/tickets``.

``status`` is absent from the shape: a ticket always opens at the beginning
of the lifecycle, so there is nothing for the client to state, and letting
it state one would be a way around the machine.
CreateTicketRequest.title: CreateTicketRequest

DealFunnelConversion.description: How much of one stage reached the next.
DealFunnelConversion.title: DealFunnelConversion

DealFunnelStage.description: How much sits in one stage of the pipeline.
DealFunnelStage.title: DealFunnelStage

DealOut.description: A deal as the API publishes it.
DealOut.title: DealOut

DealStage.description: Position of a deal in the sales pipeline.
DealStage.title: DealStage

DealSummaryOut.description: A summary, plus enough provenance for the client to trust it or not.
DealSummaryOut.title: DealSummaryOut

DeliveryAddress.description: Where a parcel is picked up from, or delivered to.
DeliveryAddress.title: DeliveryAddress

DeliveryHealthDto.description:
Health payload for the integration.

It intentionally carries no base URL, no credentials and no upstream error
text — only the facts an operator needs in order to decide whether the
dependency is healthy.
DeliveryHealthDto.title: DeliveryHealthDto

DeliveryParcel.description:
Physical dimensions the carrier prices against.

The upper bounds are what a parcel service accepts at all; anything larger
is freight, which this integration does not book.
DeliveryParcel.title: DeliveryParcel

DeliveryQuoteDto.description: A price for carrying one parcel, valid until ``expiresAt``.
DeliveryQuoteDto.title: DeliveryQuoteDto

ErrorBody.description: Machine-readable description of a single failure.
ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

ErrorResponse.description: Body returned for every non-2xx response produced by this application.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FinanceSummaryOut.description:
Body of ``GET /finance/summary``.

All four states are always present, zero-filled where nothing fell into
them: a reader comparing two periods needs the rows to line up, and a
state that vanished when it emptied would make the shape of the answer
depend on the data.
FinanceSummaryOut.title: FinanceSummaryOut

ImportStatementOut.description:
Outcome of one ``POST /finance/statements/import``.

The two numbers are what makes a repeated import legible: ``imported`` is
what was new and ``skipped`` is everything already on file. A second import
of an unchanged statement therefore reports nothing new and skips the lot,
which is the visible form of the guarantee.
ImportStatementOut.title: ImportStatementOut

InquiryClassificationOut.description: A label from the closed list, or ``unknown``, never anything else.
InquiryClassificationOut.title: InquiryClassificationOut

LinkCallRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /calls/{id}/link``.

The narrow sibling of ``PATCH``: it attaches a call to the records it
belongs to and does nothing else. Both associations are optional
individually, but at least one of them has to name a record — a request
that names neither is asking for no link at all, and answering it would
burn a version and announce a ``call.linked`` that linked nothing.

``null`` is refused rather than read as "detach". This endpoint has one
direction by design: detaching is an edit, so it goes through ``PATCH``,
where ``null`` already means "clear it". One verb that both attaches and
detaches would make ``call.linked`` in the audit trail ambiguous about
which of the two it recorded.
LinkCallRequest.title: LinkCallRequest

MatchCandidateOut.description:
An order this payment might be settling.

A candidate, not a decision: it is published precisely because the system
could not choose, and the person reading it can.
MatchCandidateOut.title: MatchCandidateOut

MatchStatusShare.description: How much of the window sits in one reconciliation state.
MatchStatusShare.title: MatchStatusShare

MatchTransactionRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /finance/transactions/{id}/match``.

Two fields and no more. The amount is not among them: it is what the bank
reported, and an endpoint that let a client restate it would be an
endpoint for making the books agree by typing.
MatchTransactionRequest.title: MatchTransactionRequest

OrderItemOut.description: One line of an order, as it was priced when it was added.
OrderItemOut.title: OrderItemOut

OrderItemRequest.description: One line as it is asked for: a product and how many of it.
OrderItemRequest.title: OrderItemRequest

OrderOut.description: A sales order with its lines.
OrderOut.title: OrderOut

OwnerPerformanceRow.description: One owner's deals and orders over the window.
OwnerPerformanceRow.title: OwnerPerformanceRow

PaymentMatchStatus.description: How far a bank transaction got towards an order it pays for.
PaymentMatchStatus.title: PaymentMatchStatus

PermissionAssignment.description: One permission granted to a role at a given breadth.
PermissionAssignment.title: PermissionAssignment

PermissionCheckOut.description:
Answer of ``GET /rbac/check/{resource}/{action}``.

``scope`` is reported alongside ``allowed`` because the client needs to know
not only whether an action is possible but on which records.
PermissionCheckOut.title: PermissionCheckOut

PermissionOut.description: One capability, at the breadth it was granted.
PermissionOut.title: PermissionOut

PermissionScope.description: Breadth of a permission grant: every record, or only owned ones.
PermissionScope.title: PermissionScope

ProductOut.description: A catalogue entry as the API publishes it.
ProductOut.title: ProductOut

ProductSortField.description:
Columns a caller may order the catalogue by.

A closed set rather than a free string: the value ends up in an ``ORDER BY``
clause, and accepting whatever arrives would make that clause caller-written
SQL. The values are the wire spelling, the service maps them to columns.
ProductSortField.title: ProductSortField

QuoteRequest.description: Everything the carrier needs in order to price one parcel.
QuoteRequest.title: QuoteRequest

ReadinessCheckReport.description: One dependency check as the readiness report publishes it.
ReadinessCheckReport.title: ReadinessCheckReport

ReadinessReport.description:
Body of ``GET /api/health/ready``, the same shape for 200 and 503.

The handler writes the body itself, so the status code can follow the
verdict; this model is what the description publishes for it, and a test
holds the two together.
ReadinessReport.title: ReadinessReport

ReconcileOut.description:
Outcome of one batch reconciliation.

``examined`` counts the lines the batch took in; the other four count
where they ended up, and they add up to it. ``unmatched`` is reported
rather than hidden because it is the honest measure of how well the rule
is working, and ``ignored`` is the outgoing money, which is examined and
filed rather than left out of the count.
ReconcileOut.title: ReconcileOut

ReleaseStockRequest.description: Body of ``POST /stock/release`` — the same shape a reservation has.
ReleaseStockRequest.title: ReleaseStockRequest

ReserveStockRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /stock/reserve``.

A reservation is always held on behalf of something, so unlike a receipt it
cannot be recorded without a reference.
ReserveStockRequest.title: ReserveStockRequest

ResolvedInquiryCategory.description:
What a caller actually receives: a known label, or the honest fallback.

``unknown`` is a member here and deliberately not a member of
``InquiryCategory``: the model is never offered it, the API can always
return it.
ResolvedInquiryCategory.title: ResolvedInquiryCategory

RoleOut.description: A role with its complete grant list.
RoleOut.title: RoleOut

SalesSummaryBucket.description: One bucket of the revenue series.
SalesSummaryBucket.title: SalesSummaryBucket

SalesSummaryTotals.description: The whole window rolled into one row.
SalesSummaryTotals.title: SalesSummaryTotals

SettingOut.description:
One setting as the API publishes it.

``updated_at`` is already a string rather than a datetime: the DTO is stored
in the cache as JSON, and a shape that survives that round trip unchanged is
one shape fewer to keep in step.
SettingOut.title: SettingOut

ShipmentDto.description: A parcel handed to the carrier, and where it currently is.
ShipmentDto.title: ShipmentDto

ShipmentStatus.description: Lifecycle of a parcel, as reported by the carrier.
ShipmentStatus.title: ShipmentStatus

StockHealthRow.description: One product-warehouse pair at or below the threshold.
StockHealthRow.title: StockHealthRow

StockLevelOut.description: Current quantities of one product in one warehouse.

quantityAvailable.description:
What the next reservation may actually take.

Derived on the way out and never stored: a third stored counter would
be one more thing that can fall out of step with the other two.
quantityAvailable.title: Quantityavailable

StockLevelOut.title: StockLevelOut

StockMovementOut.description: One entry of the append-only movement ledger.
StockMovementOut.title: StockMovementOut

SummariseDealRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /ai/summaries/deal``.

The exact, explicitly listed fields of a deal that may be sent to a
provider — an allow-list is the only reliable way to keep that promise.
SummariseDealRequest.title: SummariseDealRequest

SyncCallsOut.description:
Outcome of one ``POST /calls/sync``.

The three numbers are what makes a repeated sync legible: ``fetched`` is
what the provider offered, ``created`` is what was new, and ``skipped`` is
everything already on file. A second sync of an unchanged batch therefore
reports the same ``fetched`` with ``created`` at zero, which is the visible
form of the guarantee.
SyncCallsOut.title: SyncCallsOut

TicketChannel.description: How a support request reached the company.
TicketChannel.title: TicketChannel

TicketOut.description:
A ticket as the API publishes it.

``deletedAt`` is deliberately absent: a soft-deleted record never leaves the
service, so the flag would only ever be null on the wire.
TicketOut.title: TicketOut

TicketPriority.description: How urgently a ticket has to be answered.
TicketPriority.title: TicketPriority

TopProductRow.description: One product in the revenue ranking.
TopProductRow.title: TopProductRow

TransactionDirection.description: Whether money entered the account or left it.
TransactionDirection.title: TransactionDirection

TransitionTicketRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /helpdesk/tickets/{id}/transitions``.

The note is what the status log keeps: the machine records *that* a ticket
moved, and this is the only place an operator can say why.
TransitionTicketRequest.title: TransitionTicketRequest

TransportKind.description: Which transport is answering — the built-in stub or a real provider.
TransportKind.title: TransportKind

UpdateCallRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /calls/{id}``.

Exactly four fields are editable, and all four are associations or notes.
An absent field means "leave as is" and an explicit ``null`` means "clear
it" — which is why the service reads ``model_fields_set`` rather than the
values.
UpdateCallRequest.title: UpdateCallRequest

UpdateContactRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /contacts/{id}``.

Every field is optional and null is a value in its own right — clearing an
address is a legitimate edit. Which is why the service reads
``model_fields_set`` and not the values: an absent field means "leave as
is", an explicit null means "erase".
UpdateContactRequest.title: UpdateContactRequest

UpdateDealRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /deals/{id}``.

Every field but ``version`` is optional, and an absent field means "leave
as is" — which is why the service reads ``model_fields_set`` rather than the
values. ``contactId`` and ``expectedCloseDate`` are the two that also accept
an explicit ``null``, meaning "clear it".
UpdateDealRequest.title: UpdateDealRequest

UpdateOrderItemRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /orders/{id}/items/{itemId}``.

Only the quantity is negotiable: the snapshot price stays as it was taken.
UpdateOrderItemRequest.title: UpdateOrderItemRequest

UpdateOrderRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /orders/{id}``.

``version`` is mandatory and is not a field to update: it is the version the
client last read, and the write is rejected if the order has moved on since.
UpdateOrderRequest.title: UpdateOrderRequest

UpdateProductRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /products/{id}``.

``sku`` is deliberately absent and the model forbids unknown fields: the
identifier of a catalogue entry must stay stable for the order lines that
reference it, so an attempt to change it is refused rather than ignored.
UpdateProductRequest.title: UpdateProductRequest

UpdateTicketRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /helpdesk/tickets/{id}``.

Every field but ``version`` is optional, and an absent field means "leave as
is" — which is why the service reads ``model_fields_set`` rather than the
values. ``contactId`` and ``assigneeId`` are the two that also accept an
explicit ``null``, meaning "clear it": a ticket may legitimately belong to
nobody in particular and to no contact on file.
UpdateTicketRequest.title: UpdateTicketRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /users/{id}``.

Every field is optional, and an absent field means "leave as is" — which is
why the service reads ``model_fields_set`` rather than the values.
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UpdateWarehouseRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /warehouses/{id}``.

``code`` is accepted only so that a request repeating the current value
succeeds; a different value is refused by the service, because the code is
immutable once movements reference it.
UpdateWarehouseRequest.title: UpdateWarehouseRequest

UserRoleOut.description: A role as it appears on a user record.
UserRoleOut.title: UserRoleOut

UserSessionOut.description: One refresh grant, as shown in the account's device list.
UserSessionOut.title: UserSessionOut

WarehouseOut.description: A warehouse as the API publishes it.
WarehouseOut.title: WarehouseOut
